points.text: M1: Si is giant covalent AND S is simple molecular / has intermolecular forces.
M2: Si involves breaking covalent bonds AND S involves breaking intermolecular forces.
M3: more energy is needed to break covalent bonds than intermolecular forces OR covalent bonds are strong AND intermolecular forces are weak.
Total electrons in s subshells: Si 6, P 6, S 6.
Total electrons in p subshells: Si 8, P 9, S 10.
P has greater attraction of the nucleus for outer electrons than Si, or the converse.
P has greater nuclear charge than Si, or the converse.
S has two electrons in a 3p orbital AND this results in spin-pair repulsion.
